players.product: Automated test equipment (UltraFLEXplus, Photon 100 SiPho/CPO test, Omnyx board test) for AI compute

quarterly_data.quarter: Teradyne Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FIRST HARD SIZING OF THE CPO TEST MARKET, PLUS WHO WINS WHICH INSERTION (CEO Greg Smith): the test-equipment TAM for silicon photonics co-packaged optics is about $100 million in 2026 and is expected to be between $300 million and $700 million by 2028, reaching about a billion dollars of test equipment by 2030 (optical alignment, interface hardware and material handling are a separate TAM). Today it is 'a very concentrated market' - one customer and a very small number of devices drive most of the 2026 capital intensity. A CPO device has four major optical test insertions: (1) the photonics wafer, (2) the silicon photonics wafer with the electronic ICs bonded to it, (3) the singulated optical engine dielets with the mounting plate for FAU alignment, (4) the assembled CPO device. On this first device at this first customer, 'Advantest is strongest in insertion one, Teradyne is strongest in insertion two, a Taiwanese supplier is strongest in insertion three, and Teradyne is strongest in insertion four.' Management flags scaling pain as the reason for 'increasing excitement about copper networking for scale-up' and for NPO, which avoids the yield risk of a full CPO device.
quarterly_data.figure: CPO/SiPho test equipment TAM about $100 million in 2026, between $300 million and $700 million by 2028, about a billion dollars by 2030

quarterly_data.quarter: Teradyne Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: MERCHANT COMPUTE (GPU) SECOND-SOURCE PATH QUANTIFIED: Teradyne was invited in the middle of 2025 to qualify as a second vendor for test in a merchant compute account; the qualification part - deliberately a mature, already-ramped device so the tester was the only variable - was released in the first part of this year and is loaded in production on a small fleet of testers. Teradyne is now developing additional devices for release on both its own and the incumbent platform; those parts are earlier in their life cycle, are expected to finish in the second part of this year, and the associated production volume would be captured in 2027. Management expects to stay in this program-conversion mode 'for the next three to five years... we are going to slowly gain share up to maybe 30% of that compute portion of the account', after which share depends purely on which platform is chosen for initial part qualification.
quarterly_data.figure: share path to maybe 30% of the merchant compute portion of the account over the next three to five years; volume capture starting 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Teradyne Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CUSTOM AI SILICON - TERADYNE HOLDS BOTH CLOUD-COMPUTE HYPERSCALER ACCOUNTS AND SIZED THEM: 'there are really two very large players and a third that is at scale, but not of the same magnitude. Two of them are in cloud compute, and the other is primarily in the automotive and robotic space. Those are the three players that are loading hundreds of testers.' Teradyne has the two cloud-compute hyperscalers. At the first, which used to be exclusively on the competitor's platform, Teradyne began qualifying in 2023, succeeded in 2024, 'and by 2026, we had the majority share in that hyperscaler account'. The second at-scale cloud hyperscaler has opened a second-source slot: the first part is correlated and being released to production, follow-on devices are under way, and Teradyne expects 'to begin capturing meaningful production share in 2027'. 'Each one of these is hundreds of millions of dollars of TAM to $1 billion of TAM in any particular year.' Between the two AI franchises, the ASIC business has more 2027 upside than networking, which is a more mature, more predictable TAM.
quarterly_data.figure: majority share at the first cloud hyperscaler by 2026; meaningful production share at the second expected 2027; each account hundreds of millions of dollars to $1 billion of TAM per year

quarterly_data.quarter: Teradyne Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2027 MEMORY TEST CALL: 'modest up for HBM and strong growth for DRAM and flash in 2027' - explicitly NOT the digestion phase management had previously flagged as a risk. History given: 2024 was the initial HBM capacity ramp, where test capacity actually got ahead of production; 2025 HBM TAM was significant but basically flat year-on-year; 2026 is back to strong growth above 2025; and Teradyne's initial view of 2027 is continued growth. The 2026 upside surprise was the rest of DRAM - 'much, much stronger than we expected coming into the year' - driven by a burst of LPDDR and DDR activity tied to CPUs, SoCs and the memory needed for agentic AI. NAND is turning too: the memory market was almost 50%/50% NAND/DRAM historically and was 85% DRAM, 15% flash in 2025, with a resurgence beginning toward the end of 2026 led by eSSD and data-center solid state drives, which management expects to be an even stronger year in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027: modest up for HBM, strong growth for DRAM and flash; memory mix 85% DRAM / 15% flash in 2025 versus almost 50%/50% historically

quarterly_data.quarter: Teradyne Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: INTEGRATED SYSTEM TEST IS BEING CARRIED BY DATA-CENTER HDD - AND SSD TEST IS A NEW 2026 ENTRY: 'The most important thing that's driving our short-term results in our integrated system test group is actually traditional hard disk drive test, and that's both higher exabyte growth, but also share gain. That right now, we serve all three major manufacturers of data center class hard drives, and that's the part of the market that's growing most rapidly.' Alongside it, mobile system-level test has gained share and won additional customers in a unit-flat market, and Teradyne is building system-level test and burn-in for AI accelerators for hyperscalers and for edge AI products going into automotive (wide temperature ranges, higher quality level than traditional test). New in 2026: Teradyne is entering solid-state drive test - it previously tested hard drives and flash memories but not the SSD itself - because the transition of SSDs to PCIe 6.0 creates a discontinuity and raises test intensity.
quarterly_data.figure: serves all three major manufacturers of data center class hard drives; SSD test entered in 2026 on the PCIe 6.0 transition
